 * Fixed `BPTree` failing to construct a single-node tree ([#2618](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2618)).
 * Fixed `BPTree`'s forward search reading past the end of its range min-max tree when a search starting in the last block of parentheses found nothing, e.g. for `level_next` of the root. The results were correct, but the read is undefined, and in a GPU kernel it can fault ([#2632](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2632)).
 * Fixed `BPTree.preorder_select` counting its ranks from 0, while `preorder_rank` counts from 1, so that it did not invert `preorder_rank` (given a node's rank, it returned the next node in preorder) and read past the end of the tree's index for the last node. Ranks now count from 1 for both, as for `postorder_rank` and `postorder_select`, and both selects return -1 for a rank outside 1 to the number of nodes rather than read outside the index. The asymmetry came from the layout of the select index inherited from improved-octo-waddle, which now holds the positions of each parenthesis with no leading entry ([#2632](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2632)).
+* Fixed `BPTree`'s navigation methods recursing forever, or reading outside the tree's arrays, for a position outside the tree, such as the -1 that `parent` returns for the root (e.g. `first_child(parent(0))` hung). They now return -1 for such a position (`is_tip` and `is_ancestor` return False) ([#2635](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2635)).
+* Fixed the Numba functions of `skbio.tree.bp.numba` reading outside the tree's arrays for a position outside the tree, such as the -1 that `parent` returns for the root. They now return -1 for it (`is_tip` and `is_ancestor` return False), as the `BPTree` methods do ([#2635](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2635)).
+* Fixed `BPTree` accepting a topology array that is not a single tree, e.g. with bytes other than 0 and 1, a closing parenthesis before its opening one, or several trees in a row, which its navigation then read outside its arrays for. It now raises `ValueError`, naming the first position at fault ([#2635](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2635)).
+* `BPTree.data` of a NumPy tree is now a read-only view, as `lengths` and `edges` are, so that the topology cannot be changed under the tree's navigation index ([#2635](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2635)).
+* Fixed `BPTree.shear` looping forever on a single-node tree ([#2635](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2635)).
+* Fixed `BPTree`'s backward search of its index never finding position 0 when searching from position 1. No navigation method asked for that result, so none returned a wrong node ([#2635](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2635)).
 * Fixed `BPTree`'s Newick reader overflowing its buffer, or crashing, on valid trees with tips that have no label (e.g. `(,);`), and assigning the labels after such a tip to the wrong nodes (e.g. `(,b);` named the first tip `b`). A double quote (`"`) is now an ordinary character, as in the `TreeNode` reader, rather than a quote that could crash the reader, and input that is not a single tree, such as unbalanced parentheses or quotes, raises an error ([#2634](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2634)).
 * Fixed `BPTree`'s Newick reader taking `''` as an apostrophe only inside a fully quoted label: it now reads labels as the `TreeNode` reader does, e.g. `O''Brien` as `O'Brien` ([#2634](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2634)).
 * Fixed pickling and copying a `BPTree` losing its edge numbers ([#2634](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2634)).

+def _check_single_tree(index, size):
+    """Check that balanced parentheses describe a single tree.
+
+    The excess (opening minus closing parentheses up to each position) of a
+    single tree is at least 1 until the root closes, at the last position. The
+    navigation relies on it: it reads outside the tree's arrays otherwise.
+    """
+    i = index["root_close"]
+    if i == size - 1:
+        return
+    if index["e_index"][i] < 0:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "The topology array is unbalanced: the closing parenthesis at "
+            "position %d closes no node." % i
+        )
+    raise ValueError(
+        "The topology array describes more than one tree: the root closes at "
+        "position %d, before the end." % i
+    )
